correctness.rationale: Derivations restrict to the commutator ideal Z via induced rho(B) and have arbitrary central shear. When v!=0 every desired evaluation is attainable by choosing Bv and g(v), so locality restricts only S(z) to rho(End(V))z on pure central inputs. Decomposable bivectors imply S(u wedge v) lies in u wedge V+v wedge V. The coefficient comparison and four-index Plucker relation force S=rho(B), and rho is injective for n>=3 if 2 invertible. For n=3 the trace-transpose representation is an isomorphism. Constructive point witnesses yield converse, dimensions and semidirect bracket. The supplied checker is algebraic finite-field corroboration, not proof of arbitrary n and field.
